messages:
Maya: Heads-up — onboarding a new Llama-adapter model. HF `chat_template` that uses varargs renders into one long prompt and the assistant markers disappear in the Redwood preprocessor. Repro below.
Oliver: Can you paste the minimal HF template and the exact converted output so we can see what the preprocessor did?
Maya: Minimal HF `chat_template` (Jinja):
```jinja
{% for role,text in conversation %}
  {% if role == "system" %}<<SYS>>{{ text }}<</SYS>>
  {% elif role == "user" %}<|user|>{{ text }}<|end|>
  {% elif role == "assistant" %}<|assistant|>{{ text }}<|end|>
  {% endif %}
{% endfor %}
```
Maya: Converted Redwood prompt (what we saw in runtime):
```text
<<SYS>>system message<</SYS>><|user|>hi<|end|><|assistant|>ok<|end|>
```
Maya: Problem is the Jinja whitespace/control tags removed the newline between `<|end|>` and `<|assistant|>`, tokenizer later merges boundary in quantized tokenizer and runtime treats the assistant block as part of previous user token -> assistant role effectively lost in parsing, which triggers our eval harness to reissue user prompt (fallback loop). Evals show quality drop: winrate down ~8% vs baseline in interactive regression.
Sanjay: Hm, could be two things: (1) special tokens for `<|assistant|>` not registered in the model `config.json`/tokenizer, (2) preprocessor assumes sentinels are newline-delimited. Which tokenizer config are you shipping?
Maya: snippet from `config.json` we used: "special_tokens": { "pad_token": "<|pad|>", "eos_token": "<|end|>", "bos_token": "<|start|>" } — we never added `<|assistant|>` or `<|user|>` as additional_special_tokens.
Oliver: That will cause the tokenizer to emit subword tokens around the literal sentinel. With some normalizers (NFKC, whitespace collapse) the boundary can change after quantization. Add them as `additional_special_tokens`.
Eva: Quick checklist: add `additional_special_tokens: ["<|assistant|>", "<|user|>"]` to `config.json`, run `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)` before saving. Also ensure `normalize` flags match HF tokenizer behavior (strip_accents, lowercase).
Maya: Tried adding those, but still saw one failing case — because Jinja stripped the newline, so the tokens were adjacent with no whitespace. Redwood preprocessor expects sentinels on their own token boundary.
Sanjay: Two mitigations: (A) change templates to put sentinels on separate lines explicitly (e.g. `\n<|assistant|>\n{{ text }}`), (B) tweak Redwood converter to insert a zero-width separator or ensure tokenizer `bos/eos` mapping preserves boundaries.
Oliver: Also add a small unit test in `eng-ml` that converts a randomized conversation and asserts that the parsed role sequence equals the input role sequence. That would have caught the vararg collapse earlier.
Maya: For reproducibility I pasted the minimal repro harness: `python tests/repro_chat_template.py --template templates/bug.jinja --model ./artifact` — it prints the preprocessor output and token ids (shows merged ids for `<|end|><|assistant|>`).
Eva: We should also add an Optimize/quality alert: if evals detect role count mismatch between pre/post conversion, create a regression alert.
Oliver: Good catch. Can you open a PR with (1) config.json special token additions, (2) small preprocessor fix that preserves newline before sentinels, (3) unit test, and (4) an eval rule?
Maya: Will do. Repro branch created locally.
deploy-bot: Branch created: `wip/chattemplate-sentinel-boundary-fix` — CI queued. :rocket:
Maya: Thanks — ping me if CI shows a tokenizer failure, I'll dump token ids.
Oliver: Also note: quantized tokenizers (int8 fast paths) sometimes inline-normalize strings, so make sure tests run against quantized artifact too.
Sanjay: I'll add a short note in model-onboarding checklist: "always register chat sentinels as additional_special_tokens and validate newline boundaries in templates". :memo:
Eva: Nice. If we still see flakiness, we can fallback to an explicit role-tagging mode in Redwood preprocessor that ignores sentinel tokens and uses explicit `role:` prefixes as a last-resort deterministic parse.
Maya: Will send PR link in this thread when ready.
